topic: How much water a household really needs for 72 hours

content.hook: How much water do you really need?

slides.title: How much *water* do you really need?
slides.body: A calm, simple answer for the first 72 hours.

slides.title: The simple rule: *3 litres* a day
slides.body: Plan about 3 litres per person, per day. That covers drinking and basic food preparation. Official guidance in Europe points in the same direction.

slides.title: 72 hours means *9 litres* each
slides.body: 3 litres x 3 days = 9 litres per person. A family of four? 36 litres. That is about six large bottles of 6 litres.

slides.title: Then add a *safety margin*
slides.body: Children, pets, hot weather and illness can raise the need. Round up rather than down. Extra water never goes to waste.

slides.title: Store it *where you can carry it*
slides.body: Use sealed bottles in a cool, dark place. Check dates now and then. In an apartment, spread them over a few spots instead of one heavy stack.

slides.title: Think about *washing water* too
slides.body: Drinking water is the priority. For hygiene and flushing, keep a few extra containers. If you get a warning, fill them before the taps stop.

slides.title: Keep a *backup* option
slides.body: Water purification tablets are a light, cheap backup. Always follow the instructions on the pack. Tick it off once, then forget about it.

slides.title: Your whole *72-hour list*, in one place
slides.body: Water, food, medicine, cash and communication. Calm and practical.

content.caption:
Water is the first thing most people ask about. Good news: the maths is simple.

Plan about 3 litres per person, per day. That covers drinking and basic food preparation.

For 72 hours, that is 9 litres each.
A household of four: 36 litres.

Then add a margin. Children, pets, warm weather and illness can raise the need. Round up.

A few calm tips:
• Store sealed bottles in a cool, dark place.
• Check dates a couple of times a year.
• In an apartment, spread bottles around so nothing is too heavy to carry.
• Keep spare containers for washing water.
• Purification tablets make a light backup. Follow the pack instructions.

This is general guidance in line with civil-protection agencies such as Sweden's MSB, Germany's BBK and Poland's RCB. Your household may need more, so adjust to your own situation.

No panic needed. One afternoon of setup, and water is sorted.
